items.summary_1line: Claude Code Loop Engineering: Stop Prompting, Start Designing Autonomous Agent Workflows Tech Times
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, claude code.
items.editor_note: Shifts the framing from per-task prompting to designing reusable autonomous agent workflows ("loop engineering").

editorial.tldr: Through June, practitioners kept publishing small, shareable guardrails to keep coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) from common failure modes — first a skill pack aimed at stopping them making ML mistakes (Jun 6), then two Claude Code skills to curb over-engineering (Jun 8). The throughline is bolting reusable constraints onto agents instead of re-prompting each task.
editorial.whats_new: A Jun 22 "loop engineering" writeup argues teams should stop one-off prompting and instead design repeatable autonomous agent workflows for Claude Code — the latest in a run of practitioner techniques for steering coding agents.
editorial.why_it_matters: For platform teams the reliability lever on coding agents is increasingly external scaffolding — skills, guardrails, and workflow design — not better one-shot prompts; these are reusable, version-controllable artifacts you can standardize across a team.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run Claude Code/Codex/Cursor in production, evaluate packaging your own house rules as reusable "skills" and codifying repeatable agent loops, rather than leaning on ad-hoc prompts per task.

status.detail: An ongoing practitioner thread on steering coding agents with reusable skills and workflow design rather than ad-hoc prompts.
